verses.1: For the choirmaster. To the tune of "Mizmor." A song. A psalm.
verses.2: May God be gracious to us and bless us. May he shine his face upon us. Selah.
verses.3: May the nations learn your way, and all the earth know your salvation.
verses.4: Let the nations give praise to you, O God; let all the nations give praise to you.
verses.5: Let the nations rejoice and sing for joy, for you judge the nations with fairness, and guide all the peoples on the earth. Selah.
verses.6: Let the nations give praise to you, O God; let all the nations give praise to you.
verses.7: The land has given its produce. May God, our God, bless us.
verses.8: May God bless us, and may all the ends of the earth fear him.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 1: "To the tune of 'Mizmor'" — "Mizmor" is the Hebrew word for "psalm"; used here as the title of a musical piece.  
- v. 5: "for you judge the nations with fairness" — "mishor" is literally "straightness" or "levelness," here rendered as "fairness."
raw:
[1] For the choirmaster. To the tune of "Mizmor." A song. A psalm.  
[2] May God be gracious to us and bless us. May he shine his face upon us. Selah.  
[3] May the nations learn your way, and all the earth know your salvation.  
[4] Let the nations give praise to you, O God; let all the nations give praise to you.  
[5] Let the nations rejoice and sing for joy, for you judge the nations with fairness, and guide all the peoples on the earth. Selah.  
[6] Let the nations give praise to you, O God; let all the nations give praise to you.  
[7] The land has given its produce. May God, our God, bless us.  
[8] May God bless us, and may all the ends of the earth fear him.  
---  
Notes  
- v. 1: "To the tune of 'Mizmor'" — "Mizmor" is the Hebrew word for "psalm"; used here as the title of a musical piece.  
- v. 5: "for you judge the nations with fairness" — "mishor" is literally "straightness" or "levelness," here rendered as "fairness."
